subject: Dedicated capacity calibration & technical deep-dive — next steps and times
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity calibration & technical deep-dive — next steps and times

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking discovery with us earlier today. Quick recap from our side: Nimbus is focused on embedding multi-turn summarization across your analytics dashboards; primary constraint is consistent 50–100 QPS at p95 latency <120ms for short-to-medium prompts, and occasional bursts to 250 QPS during report runs. We flagged: routing by tenant, KV cache opportunities, and SLOs for interactive vs. batch workloads.

Next step I propose is a dedicated capacity calibration call (technical deep-dive) to align on:
- concrete throughput numbers (sustained vs. burst) and typical prompt lengths
- latency SLOs by route and tail expectations
- test harness / synthetic workload we can run against a staging endpoint
- ideal attendee list (engineering + infra + product)

Attached is a short worksheet to capture current workload shape — could you fill and return the yellow tab ahead of the call? (workload-metrics.xlsx)

Proposed times (PDT):
- Tues 9 Sep, 11:00–12:00
- Wed 10 Sep, 14:00–15:00
- Fri 12 Sep, 08:00–09:00

If none of those work, send a couple of windows that do and we’ll accommodate. Marcus (cc) will join for kernel/throughput planning and Dev will take notes on test harness integration.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
https://redwood.inference

Attachment: workload-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet stub; please return the yellow tab)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nimbus.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity calibration & technical deep-dive — next steps and times

Hi Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. The numbers you pulled match our internal estimates, though we have a couple of clarifications: sustained expected QPS is closer to 40–60 during working hours, but as you noted we have nightly batch report runs that spike to ~220–260 for ~8–12 minutes. Prompt length distribution: ~70% short (under 150 tokens), ~25% mid (150–600), ~5% long.

I’ve attached last month’s traffic dump (current-traffic-stats.csv) and routed to our infra lead for availability. Proposed times — Wed 10 Sep 14:00–15:00 PDT works best for the engineering team.

Attendees from Nimbus: me (CTO), Priya N. (infra), Alex M. (backend lead), and one product PM. Can you confirm Redwood attendees and whether you want us to share any access to a staging runner ahead of the call?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee | CTO, Nimbus Analytics
samantha.lee@nimbus.ai

Attachment: current-traffic-stats.csv (CSV stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity calibration & technical deep-dive — next steps and times

Perfect — Wed 10 Sep 14:00–15:00 PDT is on our side. Agenda suggestion (30–45 min technical deep-dive + 15–30 min action items):
1) Quick 10-min recap of workloads & SLOs (Nimbus)
2) 25-min Redwood run-through: runtime topology, batching & caching options, and quantization tradeoffs that affect p95/p99
3) 10-min test plan: staging harness, metrics, and how we’ll simulate nightly bursts
4) Next steps & ownership (A/C)

Two quick asks before the call:
- If you can pre-fill the yellow tab in the attached workbook, Marcus can sketch a capacity map ahead of time.
- Tell us if you prefer a walkthrough on real logs or a synthetic runner; we can provide an ephemeral staging endpoint for synthetic tests.

Marcus and Dev will handle the technical heavy lifting on our side. I’ll send calendar invite with the proposed agenda and a short Loom recording if useful.

—Vanessa

>

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity calibration & technical deep-dive — next steps and times

Adding notes for prep:
- I’ll prepare a draft capacity map showing instance classes and expected token throughput for: baseline sustained 50 QPS, 250 QPS 12-minute burst, and 10 QPS cold-start windows.
- Dev, can you confirm the synthetic runner options (locally generated vs. remote staging endpoint)? I prefer we offer both — run quick local microbenchmarks and provide an ephemeral staging endpoint to validate network/serialization overhead.
- Do we want to include a short smoke test script for Priya to run during the call? It’ll help us validate tail latency in real time.

I’ll join the call from 14:00–15:00 PDT.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@nimbus.ai>
